title: ci(client): type-check regression ratchet, plus the six macro-import defects it surfaced
intent: The type-check step in client_lint_build.yml ran with continue-on-error: true and a stale TODO ("400+ pre-existing type errors"), so vue-tsc could never fail the job. The measured count on main a48e9002 is 150, not 400+. Because the errors were emitted into a log nobody gated on, a reviewer of PR #290 (typescript 5.9.3 -> 6.0.3) read them as evidence the bump had broken type-checking. It had not: typescript 5.9.3 and 6.0.3 produce byte-identical error sets on the same tree. This patch converts the decorative step into a ratchet - the count may fall freely but may not rise - which is the pattern the repo already uses in ci/file_size_baseline.json and ci/router_count_baseline.json. No source files and no dependency versions are touched.

diff_articulation.what_changed: scripts/ci/check_client_type_check_ratchet.py (new) parses a vue-tsc log, counts `file(line,col): error TSxxxx` occurrences, and compares the total against a committed ceiling; it fails on any increase, names the files that rose, prints a nudge to lower the ceiling when the count falls, and supports --write-baseline for regeneration. scripts/ci/client_type_check_baseline.json (new) records total_errors 150 plus per-code and per-file breakdowns, the dual-TypeScript witness, and a note that 63 of the 150 come from an orphaned directory. client_lint_build.yml: the type-check step now tees its output to $RUNNER_TEMP/vue-tsc.log and keeps continue-on-error (it is not the gate); a new non-continue-on-error 'Type-check regression ratchet' step runs the checker and IS the gate. The stale '400+' TODO comment is replaced with the measured 150 and the reason the step stays non-gating.
diff_articulation.why_not_redundant: Nothing in the repo gated on client type errors: the only step that ran vue-tsc was continue-on-error, and no baseline file for it existed (ci/ held file_size and router_count baselines only). The ratchet is not redundant with the existing lint step either - lint is separately continue-on-error and is NOT type-aware (packages/client/.eslintrc.cjs sets no parserOptions.project, so @typescript-eslint/parser runs syntax-only and never builds a TS program), so ESLint cannot observe type errors at all.

commands_run: BASELINE EXPERIMENT on a clean worktree at main a48e9002: npm ci -> typescript 5.9.3 -> npx vue-tsc --noEmit -> exit 2, 150 errors. Then npm i -D typescript@6.0.3 -> npx vue-tsc --noEmit -> exit 2, 150 errors. comm(3) over normalized `file(line,col): error TScode` keys: 0 lines only-in-TS5, 0 lines only-in-TS6 -> the error sets are IDENTICAL and no error is attributable to the TypeScript 6 bump

npx eslint . --ext .ts,.vue --max-warnings=1200 under typescript 6.0.3 -> 34 errors / 7683 warnings, matching the numbers observed in CI; no parser crash and no @typescript-eslint unsupported-version warning
grep for parserOptions.project in packages/client/.eslintrc.cjs -> ABSENT, confirming lint is syntax-only and structurally cannot be affected by the TypeScript version
ratchet PASS path: --log <ts6 log, 150> vs ceiling 150 -> exit 0
ratchet FAIL path: synthetic +1 error appended -> exit 1, reports 150 -> 151 and names src/views/NewThing.vue 0 -> 1
anti-bless-the-void: missing log -> exit 1; empty log -> exit 1; log with no recognizable vue-tsc output -> exit 1 (a gate that passes on absent input is worse than no gate)
clean-run path: synthetic 'Found 0 errors.' log -> exit 0 plus a nudge to lower the ceiling
CI-equivalent end-to-end: exported GITHUB_WORKSPACE and RUNNER_TEMP and ran the exact command block from the workflow verbatim -> exit 0
yaml.safe_load over client_lint_build.yml -> OK; step wiring asserted: 'Type check (vue-tsc)' continue-on-error=True, 'Type-check regression ratchet' continue-on-error=False

orphan evidence: zero inbound imports to src/views/cam/headstock/ from anywhere outside that directory; router/index.ts 'WorkspaceView' hit resolves to CamWorkspaceView.vue, a different file; all 11 aliased import targets confirmed absent on disk

RE-BASELINE 2026-08-19 after main moved (typescript 6.0.3 via #290, vue-tsc ^2.1.0 -> ^3.3.10, node-version 20 -> 22): ceiling 150 -> 156. Cause isolated on ONE tree with TypeScript held at 6.0.3 -- vue-tsc 2.2.12 -> 150 errors / 0 TS2440; vue-tsc 3.3.10 -> 156 / 6 TS2440. Attributable to the vue-tsc MAJOR, not TS6 and not new source (all 4 affected files unchanged since a48e9002). Caught before merge: the un-rebased 150 ceiling would have failed the job on landing

MACRO-IMPORT FIX 2026-08-19: removed defineProps/defineEmits/defineExpose from 'vue' imports in 4 SFCs. Verified under the REAL toolchain after a full npm ci (vue-tsc 3.3.10 confirmed reinstalled from the 2.2.12 pin used during isolation - 2.2.12 does not detect TS2440 at all and would have produced a false pass): 150 errors, 0 TS2440. Set comparison: exactly the 6 TS2440 removed, 0 introduced, and the resulting set is IDENTICAL to the original vue-tsc-2 150-set (0 differences both directions). Repo-wide sweep for other macro imports: none (control: 753 files match a vue import, so the empty result is real, not a bad pattern).

architecture_scan.acknowledgement_notes: CI-only change; no source, no dependency versions, no runtime behavior. The new gate is strictly one-directional (fails only on an increase above the current measured state), so it cannot break an existing PR that adds no type errors. Deliberately NOT done in this patch: (1) fixing the 150 errors - 87 are in live code and need domain judgement, 63 are in an orphaned directory whose removal is an owner call under FEATURE_PARITY_MIGRATION_POLICY; (2) an equivalent ratchet for ESLint - the numbers are measured (34 errors / 7683 warnings against a --max-warnings=1200 threshold) but that gate needs its own baseline and end-to-end validation, and shipping a second unvalidated gate alongside a validated one would weaken both; (3) deleting src/views/cam/headstock/ - the dead-code evidence is strong (unreachable, plus imports of 11 nonexistent modules) but source deletion is an owner decision, and the baseline file records the expected post-deletion ceiling so the follow-up is mechanical. RESOLVED (was RE-BASELINE NOTE): the ceiling is 156, but 6 of those are TS2440 macro-import defects (defineProps/defineEmits/defineExpose imported from 'vue' in <script setup>, where they are compiler macros) newly surfaced by vue-tsc 3. They are real and each is a one-line fix; the baseline records this so the ceiling returns to 150 rather than the debt being blessed at 156. Now fixed under explicit owner authorization; ceiling is back to 150 and the baseline carries no TS2440. The source edit is inert at runtime - the imports were of compiler macros.
